synthesis: Seven retrieved records, appraised at abstract level; the three leads remain unverified and are not part of the certainty. Remote monitoring closes the measurement gap in the first ten days, and self-management with protocol titration improved blood pressure control at six weeks in a small trial, while readmission differences were too small to detect. Blood pressure peaks after discharge, mostly in days 3 to 6. Uptake is lower among women who need an interpreter and those without a smartphone unless loan phones and paper options are offered. Validated devices and correct cuffs matter.
gradeRationale: Two small or partly selected trials and observational studies; consistent on measurement and six-week control, imprecise for readmission, and trials excluded digitally excluded women.
summary: Seven records appraised; four claims; certainty low.
